question.text:
Match the following

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{I. FCFS} & \text{i. Optimal Waiting Time} \\
\text{II. SJF} & \text{ii. Convoy effect} \\
\text{III. Round Robin} & \text{iii. Not practical} \\
\text{IV. SRTF} & \text{iv. No Starvation}
\end{array}
$$

  1. $\text{I - ii, II - i, III - iv, IV - iii}$
     
  2. $\text{I - i, II - ii, III - iv, IV - iii}$
     
  3. $\text{I - iii, II - i, III - iv, IV - ii}$
     
  4. $\text{I - iii, II - iv, III - i, IV - i}$
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. The performance of the Round Robin scheduling algorithm depends on the size of the time quantum.
     
  2. If the time quantum is extremely small, Round Robin algorithm for scheduling can result in a large number of context switches.
     
  3. A large time quantum can make Round Robin behave more like First-Come, First-Served (FCFS).
     
  4. All of the above statements
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Which of the following statements is false for Round Robin (RR) process scheduling?

  1. RR is suitable for a time-sharing system
     
  2. RR is a preemptive scheduling algorithm
     
  3. Its turnaround time does not depend on the time quantum
     
  4. In case of RR algorithm, the priority of all the processes are same
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
$4$ processes $A,B,C,D$ have estimated burst times of $4,~5,~6,~7$ $\text{ns}$ respectively. They are scheduled in round robin fashion and the time slice is of $2$ $\text{ns}$. The processes $A,B,C,D$ arrive at the $0,~0.5,~1,~1.5$ $\text{ns}$ respectively. The order in which the processes are completed.

  1. $B,A,C,D$
     
  2. $D,A,B,C$
     
  3. $A,B,D,C$
     
  4. $A,B,C,D$
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider the following five processes: 

$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Process} & \text{Arrival Time} & \text{Burst Time} & \text{Priority} \\
\hline
P_1 & 0 & 4 & 1 \\
P_2 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\
P_3 & 2 & 1 & 3 \\
P_4 & 3 & 5 & 4 \\
P_5 & 4 & 2 & 5 \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$ 
The scheduling policy is non-preemptive priority scheduling. 

A larger priority value means higher priority. What is the average turnaround time?

  1. $7.0$ 
     
  2. $7.6$ 
     
  3. $8.6$ 
     
  4. $9.6$
question.subject: Operating System
